body:
acme-cs: Hey team — we started getting a flood of parse failures from JSON mode this morning for our billing summary endpoint. Customer sees 400 + `invalid_json` in the response body. Sample returned payload attached. request_id=rid_9f3b

acme-cs: ```
{"invoices": [
  {"id": "inv_123", "amount": 1200,},
  {"id": "inv_124", "amount": 900}
],
"cursor": "abc123"
...
```

jen: Thanks, filing triage. Can you share the SDK call + any client-side pre/post processing?

acme-cs: Just a plain REST call using our Node SDK v0.9. No transformers. Server logs show 200 from Redwood but `output_parse_error` at our side. We see trailing comma after 1200. Sometimes there's an extra partial chunk appended like `...}\n}}ERROR` in streams.

sam: Assigning to JSON-mode squad. Likely two issues: 1) model emitted trailing commas / extra characters when streaming; 2) our parser doesn't tolerate partial/stream artifacts. First step: confirm whether the model output contains the JSON intact before any post-processing.

kai: Repro plan: run the same prompt with `stream: true` and capture raw bytes. Use curl to replicate exactly: ``curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-json-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<billing-summary-prompt>"}],"stream":true}'``

kai: If raw stream contains junk after JSON, we can 1) apply a regex extraction as a safety net, 2) re-ask the model with a stricter instruction, or 3) route to a non-streaming call for deterministic output.

jen: For immediate mitigation, try `regex` cleanup before JSON.parse: extract the first top-level JSON object/array. Suggested regex (JS): ```js
const match = raw.match(/([\[{][\s\S]*[\]}])/m);
const jsonText = match ? match[1] : raw;
```
jen: Note: this can mask legitimate multi-message outputs; use only for this customer as short-term canary.

sam: Longer-term: engineer a self-heal re-ask pattern. Steps: 1) attempt regex extraction; if parse still fails, 2) call the model again with the original conversation + system prompt: "The previous response included a JSON structure but had syntax issues. Return only the corrected JSON matching the schema below, do not add commentary." Include the schema and an example. Use exponential backoff between retries (500ms, 1s, 2s) and cap at 3 attempts.

sam: Example re-ask prompt snippet: ```
System: You are a JSON-cleaner. The user previously received: <raw_output>. Return only valid JSON matching this schema: {"invoices": [{"id": "string","amount": number}], "cursor": "string"} . No code fences.
```

kai: Also suggest routing to `rwd-json-stable` (more conservative decode) for the retry call. Add header `x-rwd-canary: json-cleanup` so we can track.

ops-bot: Logged incident ticket #INC-2026, linked to rid_9f3b. Notifying infra & runtime teams.

jen: If we implement regex extraction, add telemetry: increments `repair.regex_applied` and log `repair.success` boolean and `retry_count`. That helps decide if we should make it default.

acme-cs: Quick question — can retry attempts be billed separately? We're seeing billing alerts when retries spike.

sam: Good call. Retries will count as additional token usage on hosted API. For Dedicated customers we can enable a retry budget (free retries within threshold). I'll loop in pricing if this becomes ongoing. For now we'll keep retries minimal and use canary regex only for critical flows.

kai: Repro follow-up: I ran the curl stream and captured raw bytes. Confirmed extraneous trailing `}ERROR` in ~8% of runs. Attached sample in the ticket. Next steps: 1) push a temporary runtime fix to strip terminal non-JSON bytes from stream boundary for JSON-mode models, 2) ship the re-ask pattern in the SDK as an opt-in `jsonRepair` flag, 3) alert customers with opt-in to avoid billing surprises.

jen: Action items: sam -> draft re-ask prompt + backoff logic and unit tests; kai -> add regex canary in SDK + telemetry; ops -> monitor for regressions and add routing header; sam -> coordinate pricing note for support.

acme-cs: Thanks, please keep me posted. We can enable `jsonRepair` for our account for now.

jen: Enabled `jsonRepair=true` on your account (acct_acme). We'll monitor metrics for the next 24h. If you still see parse errors, reply in this thread with rid_*. :thumbsup:

acme-cs: Confirmed fixed on a quick test. No parse errors in 20/20 calls. Will report if anything else crops up. :tada:
